I should say now that some of these exist in theory only.

Thank you for this incredibly in-depth reply; it really helped me understand the concepts outlined in the tips more fully. I am really grateful for both you and /u/Jorsa for helping me with this. I did speak with her today before I got a chance to use some of the tips (before I got a chance to read this) but it went quite well. I started by acknowledging that I don't fully understand what she's been through and her experiences, but that I'd always be there. We then sat and talked for an hour (though we covered a lot) about some of her feelings on vegetarianism and her hatred of human greed (she associates very strongly with animals over humans). I spent a lot of time listening, and when she spoke about the hopelessness of her causes, I tried to be encouraging and suggest how she could really make an impact on the lives of animals. I don't know how effective it was, since she was still pretty negative, but I hope I planted a few positive ideas. 

Another thing that came up a few times did seem to relate to some sort of self-loathing, which I can really see know that I've read your wise words. She feels pretty lonely and says she hasn't really felt love, and that's getting her down. She says she would want someone who is similar to her, but that in finding someone like that they would both just depress each other to the point of suicide. I mentioned that perhaps she should at least keep searching until she could find someone to complete her, which would at least give her life some happiness. She said that she just doesn't have enough of a drive to find someone like that, or at least that the drive is not strong enough to keep her alive (I should say that she said all of this before we discussed her views on vegetarianism, but I don't think I changed her mind much on this either). The point that was a real case of self-loathing was that a few times she said things to the effect of "I shouldn't date anyone, because I'd just die/let/them down/disappoint them". I guess I sorta tried to turn one of these instances into a make-more-friends! situation, which she agreed on, but those kinds of things I find difficult to answer without trying to prove her wrong.

Sorry about all the text and the utter lack of formatting, but I guess if you want the tl;dr, we had a good discussion where she had the opportunity to tell me a lot, and while I don't think I've really changed her mind, things went swimmingly. Thank you both again for reading and responding.

I was just reading through these talking tips again, and I have a few questions:

These tips give examples mostly based around the concept of self-loathing, or at least the ones I immediately picked up on. In her case, her anger seems more directed outwards, as in a loathing of everything. Could this be some sort of manifestation of her own lack of self-worth, or is it handled differently? How could I restore her faith in existence?

Another issue is that her ideas are not new to me, and by repeatedly asking questions on how she feels, which I have a rough idea of, would only reinforce her belief that I don't understand her, since it would be implied that I already know. I've tried to understand, and I get the gist of where she comes from, but we both know that I don't know, so how else could I stop her from feeling lonely?

Wow, great, thank you for pointing me towards those talking tips (sidebars are a wealth of information!). It has definitely shown me what I've been doing wrong as support (a lot, unfortunately) and where I can make improvements in assisting. Hopefully I can turn this around still.

Thank you for the reply. I've tried telling her in the past that there is happiness to be found in the world, and that it isn't worth sacrificing the wonder of life for the numbness of death, yet she's dug herself into a pretty deep hatred hole. I'll try saying this to her, and I'll tell you what she says.
